purpose: Triage only. Jev reads one section of law and says whether it can change a decision in the settlement chain of a market-rate NYC residential tenancy. Jev never states what the law requires; routing thresholds are owned by code (routing.json).
global_rules: Answer from the supplied state alone: state.section_text is the complete text of one section (or rule) of one legal instrument, state.instrument names the instrument and state.heading its heading.
Judge the section as written for the chain in state.chain_description, for a market-rate residential unit in New York City under New York State, New York City and federal law.
state.aperture_exclusions lists regimes that are outside the chain; a section that decides matters only for one of them is not a decision in the chain.
Do not decide what the section requires, how it applies to a case, or whether it is valid; classify only its role.
When a section mixes provisions, classify it by its strongest provision: one provision that can change the chain's decisions is enough.
The question identifier is a label; the question is in the instructions.

questions.question: What role does this section play in the settlement chain of a market-rate NYC residential tenancy?

prompt.instructions: What role does state.section_text play in the chain in state.chain_description? Choose DECIDES if the section imposes a duty, bar, deadline, amount, condition, defense, liability or consequence that can change what a landlord, managing agent, collector or tenant does or owes in that chain, for a market-rate NYC unit. Choose EXCLUDED_REGIME if it decides such matters only for a regime listed in state.aperture_exclusions. Choose NO_DECISION if it contains definitions only, is administrative, concerns other subject matter, or governs conduct outside the chain.

criteria.DECIDES: The section imposes a duty, bar, deadline, amount, condition, defense, liability or consequence that can change what a landlord, managing agent, collector or tenant does or owes in the chain, for a market-rate NYC unit.
criteria.EXCLUDED_REGIME: The section decides such matters only for an out-of-aperture regime (rent-stabilized or rent-controlled units, public, project-based or subsidized housing, Virginia, places outside NYC, commercial tenancies).
criteria.NO_DECISION: The section contains definitions only, is administrative (agency or court organization, reporting, funding), concerns other subject matter, or governs conduct outside the chain.

questions.question: Does the text impose or alter any obligation, right, deadline, amount or consequence for a party to a residential tenancy, or a person collecting from one, at or after the tenancy's end?

prompt.instructions: Does state.section_text impose or alter any obligation, right, deadline, amount or consequence for a party to a residential tenancy (landlord, managing agent, tenant, co-tenant, guarantor, successor, estate), or for a person collecting money from one, at or after the tenancy's end? Judge the text only; include general rules (time computation, delivery of notices, capacity to sue, judgment interest, enforcement, exemptions, limitations, discharge, reporting) that reach such a party.

criteria.true: The text imposes or alters an obligation, right, deadline, amount or consequence that reaches a party to a residential tenancy, or a person collecting from one, at or after the tenancy's end.
criteria.false: The text imposes nothing that reaches such a party at or after the tenancy's end (it governs other persons, other subject matter, agency or court administration, or only definitions).

state_fields.heading: section heading
state_fields.section_text: full section text as saved (up to 12,000 characters; longer sections are not sent: they go to the review queue as LONG)
state_fields.chain_description: the chain paragraph from the register brief, verbatim
state_fields.aperture_exclusions: the out-of-aperture list from the register brief, verbatim

chain_description: The chain: from facts fixed at move-in and the notice that the tenancy is ending, to the account closed (including collection, suit, judgment, enforcement and write-off, unclaimed funds, bankruptcy, death, military, disability, domestic violence, coerced debt, tax and information reporting, data and privacy, credit reporting, anti-discrimination). Scope: NY State + NYC + federal law, a MARKET-RATE unit in NYC.
aperture_exclusions: Out of aperture: rent-stabilized and rent-controlled units, public and project-based or subsidized housing, Virginia, places outside NYC, commercial tenancies.
